findings.evidence: TypeScript verifyResultProfile has no snapshot-hash argument and does not validate skill_chain_result_refs against the current Bundle/item set; verifyAttemptResult cannot forward those fences. A schema-valid bundle with input_snapshot_hash changed to 64 zeroes and a foreign Bundle/item Skill reference was accepted by TypeScript while Python rejected it. Separately, an empty-data-binding Plan supplied with catalog but no interpreter map was accepted by TypeScript and rejected by Python.
findings.impact: TypeScript clients can accept cross-RunSnapshot results, foreign Skill anchors, or partially validated Plans that the Python/Core path rejects, breaking the required language-independent contract boundary.
findings.required_fix: Mirror the Python Result/Attempt context parameters and checks in TypeScript, including snapshot hash, Bundle/item Skill anchors and incomplete-stream target uniqueness; make partial catalog/interpreter validation context fail closed regardless of data-binding count.
findings.acceptance_test: Add directed Python/TypeScript differential cases for wrong snapshot hash, foreign/stream-backed Skill refs, duplicate incomplete-stream targets, and every catalog/interpreter argument combination for both empty and populated data_bindings.

findings.evidence: TypeScript canonicalJson accepted an isolated UTF-16 high surrogate and hashJcs produced 2764166cc09846a6d36d61cd7270fbc396b08c4ba662854319ee99d193183438. Python rfc8785 rejected the identical logical value with ContractValidationError. TextEncoder silently substitutes malformed surrogate input rather than failing closed.
findings.impact: The same malformed JSON value can be rejected in Python but assigned a package/request/receipt hash in TypeScript, creating split identities and violating RFC 8785 parity.
findings.required_fix: Reject unpaired high or low surrogates in every TypeScript string and object key before canonical serialization or UTF-8 encoding.
findings.acceptance_test: Add shared vectors for lone high/low surrogates in values and keys, valid surrogate pairs and ordinary astral characters; Python and TypeScript must make identical accept/reject decisions and produce identical bytes/hashes for accepted vectors.

findings.evidence: Both SDKs accept claim-input when accepted_atoms/acceptedAtoms is absent. They also accept an authority record that omits both current and accepted because only explicit false is rejected. Both buildClaimInputAsset implementations call verification without any authority input.
findings.impact: A rejected, superseded or otherwise non-current Atom can be deterministically sealed into the parameters Asset and RunSnapshot, so a Layer B Claim need not reverse-link to a current accepted Atom as frozen design requires.
findings.required_fix: Require an authoritative Atom set/resolver for Claim sealing and require current===true, accepted===true plus exact atom_id, payload_hash, acceptance_ordinal and source revision equality. Keep any purely structural parser explicitly separate from the authority-sealing API.
findings.acceptance_test: Reject absent authority, missing flags, false flags, unknown Atom, stale payload/ordinal and cross-Revision authority; accept only a complete exact current+accepted record and verify the resulting Asset hash remains bound to RunSnapshot.parameters_asset_id.

findings.evidence: Each files.sha256 describes 16 package files, but package_hash/release_id are calculated from a separate 13-file identity_files list. The excluded files include the executable Wheel, descriptor.json and identity.json. Anthropic declared 2771aaca... while the canonical digest of its committed full manifest is eb0b5356...; Gemini declared 01281497... versus 807fba62.... Gate and tests explicitly validate only the subset.
findings.impact: Installable code or descriptor bytes can change without changing the package_hash/release_id carried by Generation and provenance receipts, defeating package pinning, rollback and receipt identity.
findings.required_fix: Use one non-self-referential package layout in which the exact file map that generates files.sha256 also generates package_hash/release_id. Generated identity metadata must be derived or moved outside the hashed payload rather than introducing identity_files as a second authority.
findings.acceptance_test: Assert that digest_package(manifest_files).files_sha256 equals committed files.sha256 and its package/release values equal descriptor, Generation and receipt values. Mutating every installable payload, especially the Wheel and descriptor, must change identity or fail installation.

findings.evidence: Accepted Core semantics require next_offset=null when a range reaches EOF. Both providers instead require next_offset==len(data), and both mocks always return offset+len(chunk). A Host returning the committed contract-compliant EOF response passed public RPC schema validation but both providers returned ASSET_READ_ERROR.
findings.impact: The request_asset_id invocation path is incompatible with a conforming Core Host; deterministic mocks hide the incompatibility, so real provider invocations can fail before schema validation or upstream execution.
findings.required_fix: Implement contiguous paged Asset reads following Core next_offset semantics until null, verify each chunk hash/offset, and make both mocks emit null at EOF and chunk hashes consistent with the public Asset contract.
findings.acceptance_test: Run both providers against the committed EOF fixture and a multi-page Asset fixture; valid null EOF must succeed, while skipped/backward offsets, premature null, bad chunk hashes and trailing pages must fail closed.
